history.summary: Kali Bari Temple is one of Shimla's oldest Hindu temples, founded by a Bengali Brahmin named Ram Charan Brahmachari (spelled 'Bhramachari' in some sources) — the founding year is given as 1823 in one source and 1845 in several others (CONFLICT — verify), with one travel page claiming only '100 years ago'. It was originally built on Jakhoo Hill (near Rothney Castle) and was later shifted by the British rulers to its present site on Bantony Hill near Mall Road. The main deity is Goddess Kali worshipped as Shyamala in a blue wooden idol; the name 'Shimla' is popularly said to derive from 'Shyamala'. The complex also has shrines to Shiva, Ganesha and Saraswati, and idols of many goddess forms (Bhadrakali, Chinnamasta, Tara, Chamunda, Rudrarani, Durga, Himavati, Kamakhya, Kumari Sati, Meenakshi, Uma). A temple trust with Bengali members was formed in 1902; Swami Vivekananda, Rabindranath Tagore and Mahatma Gandhi are recorded as visitors. The temple runs a pre-bookable dharamshala-style accommodation and a canteen.

town_description: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh and was the summer capital of British India, set in the Shivalik Hills at about 2,200 metres. The town centres on the Ridge and Mall Road, with colonial-era landmarks like Christ Church and the Viceregal Lodge, and is linked to Kalka by the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla toy train. It is Himachal's main hill-station tourist hub, famous for Himalayan views, apple country around it, and a cluster of well-known temples.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism — Kali worship in Bengali tradition)

travel.railway: Shimla Railway Station — about 1.5 km; Shimla Old Bus Stand — about 1.6 km
travel.road: On Bantony Hill near Mall Road in the heart of Shimla; walkable from the Ridge and Mall Road, or a short taxi ride

visitor_information.best_time: April to June (summer) and September to November (autumn); Durga Puja, Navratri and Kali Puja are the most festive times
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): most sources list 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily; one source says 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM; a 2026 YouTube vlog says 5:30 AM to 9:00 PM. No entry fee
